acceptance_checks: A verdict marking a blocking item insufficient_evidence with an 'already blocked' style reason is rejected by the enforcer.
A verdict whose blocking items are all evaluated is accepted regardless of its verdict value.
The prompt instructs the judge to evaluate every blocking item even when one already fails.
Mutation guard: removing the new rejection makes at least one test fail.
non_goals: Changing the verdict enum or the CCA turn budget

findings.detail: git diff main...HEAD includes mergegate_check.py, shiki_runtime.py, ADR 0015, CONTEXT.md, and dozens of .shiki records from PRs #181-#187 that are unrelated to this task's four locked files. This is the documented stale-local-base condition, not a change authored by this task; MergeGate computes its base from origin/main where these commits already exist, so they resolve empty. Non-blocking, but the PR should ideally be rebased on current origin/main so the reviewable diff is only the four task files.
findings.title: Diff carries foreign already-merged mirror/code state (stale-local-main base)

findings.detail: _is_already_blocked_reason relies on phrase markers, so a verdict could still evade detection by marking a blocking item not_applicable, or by wording an 'already blocked' reason without any marker. Conversely a legitimate reason containing a standalone phrase like 'already determined' (e.g. 'the value was already determined upstream, so no local evidence exists') would be flagged. The task contract explicitly scopes the rejection to insufficient_evidence + 'already blocked' phrasing, the near-miss genuine reasons are well-covered by the AND-combination guard, and the mutation-guard test protects the behavior, so this is an accepted limitation rather than a defect.
findings.title: Short-circuit detection is heuristic text-matching (inherent, bounded limitation)

scope: Observed on PR #179: with CCA-08 already failing, the CCA judged that the verdict was determined and stopped, returning seven acceptance criteria as insufficient_evidence in 1m30s where an earlier run had evaluated the same criteria in detail. The verdict was right and the evidence record was hollow. Because complete requires every blocking criterion to pass, a short-circuited run can never become complete, and the record is systematically thin exactly when a blocker exists — which is most of the time. Require the prompt and the verdict enforcer to evaluate every blocking checklist item and acceptance criterion regardless of an already-known blocker, and reject a verdict that returns blocking items as insufficient_evidence with 'already blocked' as the reason.
test_command: bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
title: Require the CCA to evaluate every blocking item
